verdicts.topic: Reserve Bank of India: Foreign Exchange Reserves (End-March 2024)

facts.quote: Indias foreign exchange reserves stood at USD 640.3 billion as of the end of March 2024
facts.context_window: External Sector Overview, Paragraph 1.58 on Page 37

facts.quote: Foreign exchange reserves stood at USD 651.5 billion as at end-March 2024
facts.context_window: Economic Review - External Sector on Page 90

verdicts.summary: Genuine / likely contradiction in reported End-March 2024 Forex Reserves: USD 640.3B (Economic Survey) vs USD 651.5B (RBI).
verdicts.explanation: Both reports cite the exact same institution (RBI), metric (Foreign Exchange Reserves), and balance sheet cutoff date (End-March 2024), but diverge by $11.2 Billion. While this stems from differing cut-off publication dates (provisional weekly BoP reporting vs audited balance sheet valuation adjustments), it functions as a genuine cross-document conflict in published official figures.
verdicts.audit_notes: Flagged as Genuine / Likely Contradiction. Requires inspecting the RBI balance sheet notes to confirm currency revaluation reserves.

verdicts.topic: Indian Economy: Consumer Price Inflation FY24

facts.quote: Retail headline inflation, as measured by the change in the Consumer Price Index averaged 5.4 per cent in FY24
facts.context_window: Prices and Inflation Section on Page 28

facts.quote: Core inflation declined significantly to 3.4 per cent in FY24

verdicts.summary: Apparent contradiction in FY24 CPI inflation (5.4% vs 3.4%) resolved by Headline vs Core basket scope.
verdicts.explanation: The Economic Survey reports both 5.4% and 3.4% for FY24 inflation. The epistemic engine reconciles the apparent contradiction through scope: 5.4% is the Headline CPI (which includes volatile food and energy prices), whereas 3.4% is Core CPI (which filters out food and fuel).
verdicts.audit_notes: Resolved via consumer price basket scope: Headline vs Core.

verdicts.topic: Government of India: Fiscal Deficit (% of GDP) FY24

facts.quote: General government fiscal deficit remained elevated at 8.2 percent of GDP in FY2023/24
facts.context_window: Fiscal Policy Review, Paragraph 12 on Page 18

facts.quote: Central Government fiscal deficit for FY24 stood at 5.6 per cent of GDP
facts.context_window: Fiscal Developments and Budgetary Trends on Page 24

verdicts.summary: Apparent contradiction in FY24 fiscal deficit (8.2% vs 5.6%) resolved by General Government vs Central Government perimeter.
verdicts.explanation: IMF states the fiscal deficit is 8.2% of GDP, while the Economic Survey reports 5.6%. This stark difference is resolved by institutional perimeter: the Economic Survey measures the Central Government deficit alone, whereas the IMF reports the General Government deficit (consolidating Central Government + all 28 State Governments).
verdicts.audit_notes: Resolved via fiscal scope: General Government vs Central Government.

verdicts.summary: Extraction / reasoning failure: Macroeconomic table column slippage between Real GDP and GDP Deflator.
verdicts.explanation: On Page 64 of the IMF Article IV excerpt, a dense memorandum table places 'Real GDP growth (6.5%)' directly adjacent to 'Inflation (GDP deflator; 3.1%)'. A naive text regex or OCR column alignment matched the label 'Real GDP' with the adjacent deflator column value '3.1%', erroneously reporting that Indian GDP growth crashed to 3.1%.
